title: Values Only One List Has
statement:
You get two integer arrays, a and b. Return a pair of lists [onlyA, onlyB]:

  • onlyA holds every distinct value that appears in a but nowhere in b.
  • onlyB holds every distinct value that appears in b but nowhere in a.

Each value appears once in its list, even if it repeats in the input. The values inside each list may be in any order, but the pair itself must be [onlyA, onlyB] in that order.

examples.why: 1 is in both lists. 4 appears twice in a but is listed once.
Both arrays hold the same set of values, so nothing is unique to either side.
-5 and 5 are different values; nothing is shared.

hints: For each value of a you ask: is it anywhere in b? What structure answers that in O(1)?
Turn both arrays into sets. Sets also remove the repeats for free.
Keep the values of set A that are not in set B, and the other way round.

explain.intuition:
The question "is this value in the other list?" is a membership test. Scanning the other array each time costs O(m) per value. A set answers it in O(1), and it also collapses repeats, which the output needs anyway.

This is the same move as diffing two lists of IDs in a frontend, for example which selected items were added or removed since the last render: build a set of each side, then filter.
pitfalls: Filtering the raw arrays instead of the sets, which lists a repeated value more than once.
Swapping the two lists in the result. The order of the pair matters even though the order inside each list does not.

solutions.title: Scan the other array for each value
solutions.idea: For each value check the other array with a linear search, and skip values already added.

solutions.title: Two sets
solutions.idea: Sets give O(1) membership and drop repeats.

followups: Both arrays are already sorted. Can you do it with O(1) extra space?
The values are known to be in -1000..1000. How could a plain array replace the sets?
